title: Book 1 — Clio, Chapter 159
paragraphs: When the Cymeans heard this, they did not want to be destroyed for surrendering Pactyas or besieged for sheltering him. So they sent him to Mytilene. But when Mazares demanded his surrender from Mytilene, the Mytilenaeans were preparing to hand him over for a price. (I cannot say the exact amount because the deal was never completed.) When the Cymeans learned this, they sent a boat to Lesbos and took Pactyas to Chios instead. But he was dragged from the sanctuary of Athena Poliouchos by the Chians, who surrendered him. The price for handing him over was the district of Atarneus on the Mysian mainland, opposite Lesbos. The Persians received Pactyas and kept him under guard to present to Cyrus. For a long time after this, no Chian would use barley meal from Atarneus in any offering to any god, and nothing grown there was used in any sacred rite. Everything from that district was excluded from all their temples.
